references.text: The first instruction regarding voluntary offerings for the sanctuary, where the Lord instructs Moses to receive gifts from everyone who has a willing heart.
Moses conveys the Lord's command to bring voluntary offerings, in the same context as verse 29.
Describes how the people brought voluntary offerings with hearts that moved them to do so, parallel to the description in verse 29.
Continuation of the collection of voluntary offerings, where the people brought so much that Moses had to stop them.
David praises God because the people gave willingly and joyfully for the temple, reflecting the same principle of a willing heart.
David acknowledges that the ability to give voluntarily comes from God, connected to the theme of voluntary offerings.
Kore was responsible for the voluntary offerings to God, continuing the tradition of voluntary sacrifices.
Paul teaches that a gift is acceptable according to what one has, when the will is present—the same principle of the willing heart.
Each person should give as they have decided in their heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver—a New Testament parallel to voluntary giving.
Describes the same collection event where the people's voluntary offerings (35:29) led to an abundance that required the work to be stopped (36:3).
Highlights the connection between the people's voluntary offerings (35:29) and the complete obedience that characterized the entire building project (39:42).
Connects the collection phase of voluntary offerings (35:29) with the final completion of the work (39:32).
